Vesicles
Glyoxysomes: specialized peroxisomesfound on seeds of some plants
Break down stored fatsto provide energy for developing plant embryo
Endosome: results when a cell engulfs material by surrounding it with the plasma membrane, then pocket formed buds off to become vesicle within cell
Lysosomes can fuse with endosomes to digest engulfed material
Food vacuole: stores nutrients
explanation: This slide describes several specific types of vesicles. Glyoxysomes are specialized peroxisomes found in the seeds of certain plants; they function to break down stored fats to supply energy for the developing plant embryo. An endosome is a vesicle that forms when a cell engulfs extracellular material by surrounding it with its plasma membrane, which then pinches off internally. Lysosomes can fuse with these endosomes to digest the engulfed contents. A food vacuole is another type of vesicle whose primary function is to store nutrients.

questions.q: What is the function of glyoxysomes in the seeds of some plants?
opts: They perform photosynthesis to produce glucose.
They break down stored fats to provide energy for the developing plant embryo.
They form endosomes by engulfing external proteins.
They synthesize cell walls during cell division.
questions.exp: Glyoxysomes are specialized peroxisomes found in some plant seeds that break down stored fats to provide energy for the developing plant embryo.
